title: Seesaw Loss for Long-Tailed Instance Segmentation
mechanism: Per class pair, mitigate negative gradients that frequent classes put on rare classes and compensate when the rare class is wrongly predicted.
adaptation: Pixel-wise softmax version: background, ribbons, busbar suppress splice at every pixel; crack vs inactive pair benefits from compensation.
min_experiment: Arm: seesaw CE replacing CE, 3 seeds; baseline SUP100; metric mIoU_rob and splice IoU; kill if mIoU_rob < +0.01.
evidence: R: LVIS long-tailed instance segmentation, gains on rare categories (abstract level).
